publication.title: Coupled Transcriptomic and ECM-Mechanical Remodeling Reveal Mechanotransductive Pathways in Spinal Cord Injury

observed_mechanical_trajectory.observation: progressive stiffening with denser fibrotic ECM and prolonged relaxation dynamics

transcriptomic_alignment.chronic_stiff_phase: collagen synthesis, ECM organization and fibrotic-remodeling programs enriched
transcriptomic_alignment.mechanotransduction: regulators change in temporally coordinated fashion with tissue-mechanics evolution
transcriptomic_alignment.boundary: temporal co-variation does not establish mechanics as the causal driver of the transcriptomic state

clock_consequence.best_supported_natural_history: SCI mechanics are non-monotonic: early softening precedes later chronic scar stiffening
clock_consequence.importance_for_delayed_retuning: a future delayed mechanical intervention must be anchored to measured lesion mechanics rather than chronological injury time alone

anti_heuristic_boundaries: The one-month stiffness minimum is not declared a therapeutic optimum.
The six-month stiffening phase is not declared causally sufficient for regenerative failure.
Bulk RNA programs are not lineage-resolved scar-cell EXIT.
A natural-history time series cannot substitute for a delayed intervention root.
No modulus threshold is inferred from the published trajectory.
next_exact_test: Perform delayed endogenous lesion retuning at prespecified mechanically defined phases, with lesion mechanics measured immediately before and after retuning, lineage/state-resolved scar-cell trajectory, and locomotor/sensory outcome in the same causal root.
